neighbours.label: demonstrative 'that' (or 'the') pointing back to an event noun just named, right before the noun is repeated ('...before the Notre Dame game, sidelining him for that game')
fire: She twisted her knee before the Stanford game, which kept her on the bench for that game.
He was sick before the Boston race and had to withdraw from that race entirely.
The goalkeeper was injured ahead of the Chelsea match, ruling him out for that match.
Rain fell throughout the Sunday concert, and attendance at that concert was poor.
He broke a finger prior to the Michigan game, sidelining him for that game.
She fell ill before the Paris tournament and never played in that tournament.
The pitcher strained his elbow before the Tuesday start and was scratched from that start.
A storm hit just before the Oakland game, delaying kickoff for that game by an hour.
quiet: She twisted her knee in training, which kept her on the bench for three weeks.
He was sick in the spring and had to withdraw from racing entirely.
The goalkeeper was injured in the warm-up, ruling him out for a month.
Rain fell throughout Sunday, and attendance was poor.
He broke a finger in practice, sidelining him for six weeks.
She fell ill in Paris and never played again.
The pitcher strained his elbow on Tuesday and was scratched from the lineup.
A storm hit Oakland in the evening, delaying kickoff by an hour.

notes: Probes: 'for that game' 1.25, 'for that match' 0.39, 'in the image' (after Instagram photo) 0.63, 'praised the book' (after novel) 0.24, but 'in the clip' 0.06. A second trigger was not tested here: range slots 'from economy to luxury' 0.82, 'from budget to deluxe' 0.61. The + pole fires on ' new' before 'ones' and the output promotes ' ones', so this pole may mark 'the specific noun comes next, not a pro-form'.
